## Overview Adds a `--dbo-scope {all,prefill}` option (`ParallelConfig.dbo_scope`) so users can choose which batches Dual Batch Overlap runs on. The default `all` keeps today's behavior. `prefill` only microbatches batches that contain a prefill. Decode-only batches always run as a single batch, and no microbatched decode CUDA graphs are captured. ## Claims - **New option:** `--enable-dbo --dbo-scope prefill` turns on DBO for prefill batches only. `--dbo-scope all` (the default) behaves exactly like current `--enable-dbo`. - **No ubatched decode graphs under `prefill`:** microbatched decode CUDA graphs are not captured, which saves capture time and graph memory. - **One decision point:** the scope is applied in `check_ubatch_thresholds()`, which every path already uses to decide whether to microbatch: - V1 runner DP sync and CUDA graph capture. - V2 runner DP sync and CUDA graph candidates. - **Backward compatible and platform-agnostic:** `--enable-dbo` is unchanged, and the default keeps current behavior on every backend. ## Validation **Unit tests:** `tests/v1/worker/test_dbo_scope.py` (new, CPU-only). ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_dbo_scope.py tests/v1/worker/test_ubatch_offsets.py -q # 21 passed ``` The new tests cover: - `check_ubatch_thresholds` for each scope, decode vs. prefill batches, and token counts just above and below the thresholds: - `prefill` never microbatches a uniform-decode batch, even at 1M tokens. - Prefill batches still follow `--dbo-prefill-token-threshold` under both scopes. - `all` keeps the existing decode threshold behavior. - Nothing is microbatched when DBO is off. - V2 CUDA graph candidates: a FULL uniform-decode descriptor (64 reqs × 4 tokens) gets a microbatched twin under `all` and none under `prefill`. - CLI and config: - The default is `all`. - `--dbo-scope prefill` and `--dbo-scope all` are passed through to `EngineArgs`. - Unknown values (e.g. `decode`) are rejected by argparse. ## Details **Motivation.** DBO hides one microbatch's communication behind the other microbatch's compute. For that to pay off, communication must be a large share of the step and each microbatch must have enough compute to cover it. Prefill batches meet both conditions. Decode batches often don't, particularly in single-node DP/EP deployments where communication is cheap (e.g. 8 × MI355X with `allgather_reducescatter`). *Little to gain:* - **Decode communication is mostly fixed latency.** Each rank sends only tens to hundreds of tokens per layer, so all-gather / reduce-scatter time is dominated by launch and sync latency, not bandwidth. Splitting into two microbatches pays that latency twice and does not halve communication time. - **Little compute to hide it behind.** Each decode microbatch's MoE and attention work takes only tens of microseconds, often too short to cover the other microbatch's communication. *Real costs:* 1. **MoE weights are read twice.** Decode MoE GEMMs are bound by memory bandwidth, so their cost is mostly reading expert weights. With two microbatches, an expert activated in both is read from HBM twice, nearly doubling weight traffic. Prefill is compute-bound and amortizes weight reads over many tokens, so it isn't affected. 2. **Lower GPU utilization.** Halving an already small batch cuts the parallelism of attention/MLA and GEMM kernels, leaving compute units underused. 3. **Fixed per-step overhead.** Switching between microbatch threads, event waits between the compute and comm streams, two sets of attention metadata and twice the kernel launches cost the same regardless of batch size. That overhead is a much larger share of a short decode step than of a prefill step. 4. **Padding waste.** Microbatching is all-or-none across DP ranks, which are padded to the same token count, and CUDA graphs add padding to align both microbatches to capture sizes. On small decode batches that padding is a large fraction of the work. 5. **Extra CUDA graphs.** A second set of microbatched FULL decode graphs has to be captured, adding startup time and graph memory. 6. **MTP amplifies all of the above.** With 3 speculative tokens, each decode request carries 4 tokens, so the default `--dbo-decode-token-threshold` of 32 already splits a rank with just 8 requests. Decode state under MTP + DBO is also more involved, and per-microbatch draft state is easy to get wrong (see the MTP hidden-buffer offset fix in #57773). In our DeepSeek-V4-Pro DP8 + MTP runs on MI355X, the DBO gain (+7% output throughput, −3.5% TPOT vs. no DBO) was measured with decode microbatching effectively disabled (`--dbo-decode-token-threshold 8192`). We have not yet run a dedicated decode-DBO on/off comparison; `--dbo-scope` makes that A/B a one-flag change. Decode DBO can still win when communication is expensive or the batch is large: - multi-node EP, where cross-node all-to-all is costly; - very large decode batches per rank; - DeepEP low-latency kernels designed for decode overlap. So the default stays `all`. Today the only way to keep DBO on prefill alone is to set `--dbo-decode-token-threshold` to a very large value. That is indirect, easy to get wrong when MTP multiplies the decode token count, and hard to read in deployment recipes. `--dbo-scope prefill` states the intent directly. **Design.** - The option is a new field rather than a value on `--enable-dbo`, so existing configs and the Python API (`enable_dbo: bool`) don't change. - The check lives in `check_ubatch_thresholds()`, which every runtime and capture path already calls. Nothing else needs to change: - V1 capture only builds ubatched graphs when this function returns True for a uniform decode batch. - V2's `_maybe_ubatch_twin()` asks it with `uniform_decode=True`. - `dbo_scope` is included in `ParallelConfig.compute_hash()` like the existing DBO thresholds, so DP ranks with different scopes are caught by the config hash check. **Semantics.** "Decode" means a uniform decode batch: every request has the same query length (1 + number of speculative tokens). This is the same split `--dbo-decode-token-threshold` and `--dbo-prefill-token-threshold` already use. Non-uniform decode-only batches stay on the prefill side and follow the prefill threshold. DP consistency is unchanged. Microbatching is still decided all-or-none across DP ranks from the synced uniform-decode flag, so all ranks reach the same answer. **Limitations.** Only `all` and `prefill` are offered. A `decode`-only scope can be added later if there's a use case. ---

@@ -29,10 +29,11 @@ Below is the overlap schedule that is currently implemented in vLLM.
 
 ## Running with DBO
 
-To enable the DBO system pass in the `--enable-dbo` argument to your vllm serve command. This must be run in conjunction with `--data-parallel-size N` where N is greater than 1 and `--enable-expert-parallel`. Additionally, there are two configuration knobs.
+To enable the DBO system pass in the `--enable-dbo` argument to your vllm serve command. This must be run in conjunction with `--data-parallel-size N` where N is greater than 1 and `--enable-expert-parallel`. Additionally, there are three configuration knobs.
 
 * `--dbo-decode-token-threshold` the minimum number of tokens in a decode-only batch required to enable DBO for that batch
 * `--dbo-prefill-token-threshold` the minimum number of tokens in a batch containing at least one prefill required to enable DBO for that batch
+* `--dbo-scope` the batches DBO applies to: `all` (default) microbatches both prefill and decode batches, `prefill` only microbatches batches containing at least one prefill
 
 Currently, DBO is only supported with DeepEP, so DeepEP must be installed and the `--all2all-backend` argument must be set to `deepep_low_latency` if your workload is primarily decode requests, or `deepep_high_throughput` if your workload is primarily prefill requests.

@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for ``--dbo-scope``, which limits DBO to prefill or all batches."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.config import ParallelConfig
+from vllm.config.compilation import CUDAGraphMode
+from vllm.engine.arg_utils import EngineArgs
+from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils import (
+    BatchExecutionDescriptor,
+    CudaGraphManager,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.ubatch_utils import check_ubatch_thresholds
+
+DECODE_THRESHOLD = 32
+PREFILL_THRESHOLD = 512
+
+
+def _config(dbo_scope: str, use_ubatching: bool = True) -> SimpleNamespace:
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        use_ubatching=use_ubatching,
+        num_ubatches=2,
+        dbo_scope=dbo_scope,
+        dbo_decode_token_threshold=DECODE_THRESHOLD,
+        dbo_prefill_token_threshold=PREFILL_THRESHOLD,
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dbo_scope", ["all", "prefill"])
+def test_prefill_batches_follow_threshold(dbo_scope: str):
+    config = _config(dbo_scope)
+    assert check_ubatch_thresholds(config, PREFILL_THRESHOLD, uniform_decode=False)
+    assert not check_ubatch_thresholds(
+        config, PREFILL_THRESHOLD - 1, uniform_decode=False
+    )
+
+
+def test_scope_all_microbatches_decode():
+    config = _config("all")
+    assert check_ubatch_thresholds(config, DECODE_THRESHOLD, uniform_decode=True)
+    assert not check_ubatch_thresholds(
+        config, DECODE_THRESHOLD - 1, uniform_decode=True
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [DECODE_THRESHOLD, 8192, 1 << 20])
+def test_scope_prefill_never_microbatches_decode(num_tokens: int):
+    config = _config("prefill")
+    assert not check_ubatch_thresholds(config, num_tokens, uniform_decode=True)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dbo_scope", ["all", "prefill"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("uniform_decode", [True, False])
+def test_no_microbatching_without_dbo(dbo_scope: str, uniform_decode: bool):
+    config = _config(dbo_scope, use_ubatching=False)
+    assert not check_ubatch_thresholds(config, 1 << 20, uniform_decode=uniform_decode)
+
+
+def test_parallel_config_default_scope_is_all():
+    assert ParallelConfig().dbo_scope == "all"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("cli_args", "expected"),
+    [
+        ([], "all"),
+        (["--dbo-scope", "prefill"], "prefill"),
+        (["--dbo-scope", "all"], "all"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_cli_dbo_scope(cli_args: list[str], expected: str):
+    parser = EngineArgs.add_cli_args(FlexibleArgumentParser())
+    args = parser.parse_args(["--enable-dbo", *cli_args])
+    engine_args = EngineArgs.from_cli_args(args)
+    assert engine_args.enable_dbo
+    assert engine_args.dbo_scope == expected
+
+
+def test_cli_rejects_unknown_dbo_scope():
+    parser = EngineArgs.add_cli_args(FlexibleArgumentParser())
+    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
+        parser.parse_args(["--dbo-scope", "decode"])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("dbo_scope", "expect_twin"), [("all", True), ("prefill", False)]
+)
+def test_ubatched_decode_graph_candidates(dbo_scope: str, expect_twin: bool):
+    """Prefill scope captures no microbatched decode CUDA graphs."""
+    manager = SimpleNamespace(
+        ubatch_runner=object(),
+        vllm_config=SimpleNamespace(parallel_config=_config(dbo_scope)),
+    )
+    # 64 decode requests with 3 speculative tokens each.
+    desc = BatchExecutionDescriptor(
+        cg_mode=CUDAGraphMode.FULL, num_tokens=256, num_reqs=64
+    )
+    twin = CudaGraphManager._maybe_ubatch_twin(manager, desc)
+    assert (twin is not None) == expect_twin
